_comment: Config for shared-build-tools/check-wporg-rejection-classes.php. 'cloudscale' is the shared-library prefix (CloudScale_Telegram/CloudScale_Licence come from cloudscale-backup).
legacy_prefixes_reason: 'csdt' is cyber-devtools' prefix, and one option written from this plugin carries it: csdt_alert_env_label, in the shared CloudScale_Telegram class. That is deliberate and documented at the top of shared-admin-ui/class-cloudscale-telegram.php -- the Telegram token, chat id, mute switch, rate ledger and environment label are ONE configuration for the whole five-plugin suite, only one copy of the class ever loads, and prefixing them per-plugin would split one config into five. A migration from the older cloudscale_* names to csdt_* is in flight (every read falls back, every write updates both), so renaming this one would move it backwards against that migration and orphan the setting on every site that has one. Declared here rather than under finding_budget because it is the tighter statement: only a csdt_-prefixed name counts, and only one of them.
path_accessor_reason: The only shipped file that may read a core path constant. This plugin needs two locations and had four reads of them: the install root, to complete a wp-content/uploads/ URL whose host has been stripped when checking whether an in a post still has a file behind it; and the content directory, for the three Site Health disk metrics, which are measured at wp-content rather than at uploads on purpose -- uploads can sit on another partition, and the number reported is about the partition this plugin's cleanup frees space on. It returns core's own value whenever the constant is defined and derives only as a fallback: a disk metric taken at a path core disagrees with is a wrong number reported confidently, and a file-existence check against the wrong root deletes the wrong thing.
_finding_budget_note: Empty, and deliberately PRESENT rather than removed: with the key here any new finding of any class fails the build immediately. The 3 runtime-config entries it used to hold were the @set_time_limit(120) calls in the thumbnail-regen, media-recycle and image-optimise handlers, all removed 2026-08-19 in favour of a host-derived wall-clock budget (cscc_chunk_deadline) plus crash-safe commit ordering. NOTE: --tighten cannot clear a stale budget once a plugin is clean, because the checker exits on its clean path before reaching the ratchet; this was set by hand.
